key_insight: The paper shows that coalition bargaining can be simulated with LLM agents by combining partisan persona training, manifesto-grounded retrieval, and provenance tracking to explain who shaped the final agreement.
engineering_relevance: It offers a transparent multi-agent architecture for politically constrained negotiation systems, with auditability mechanisms that can be reused in other high-stakes decision-support workflows.
method: SFT and DPO create strong party-specific agent personas.
Per-party RAG constrains each agent to its official manifesto.
A formateur arbitrates hub-and-spoke negotiation, while MILT and CIS trace and score clause provenance.
evidence_signal: Across three independent simulations on the 2019 Flemish election, the framework produced a stable party ranking and showed that manifesto-anchored clauses aligned with the real coalition agreement better than hallucinated content.
watch_item: Results depend on manifesto quality, retrieval fidelity, and the assumption that simulated party behavior can be faithfully represented by LLM personas.
paper_title: Digital Pantheon: Simulating and Auditing Coalition Formation with LLM Agents
